messages:
Maria Gomez: FYI, bringing up spectral-7b (int4) in the canary pool and running the codegen eval. Seeing a ~6% BLEU regression vs fp16 baseline and intermittent OOMs on 32GB A100 when batch_size >= 4. Repro below.

Maria Gomez: Repro command (canary run id 483):
``
redwood-canary run --model spectral-7b --quant=int4 --batch_size=4 --max_new_tokens=256 --eval codegen-smoke
logs: s3://redwood-canary/483/logs.txt
```

infra-bot: Canary 483 finished — exit=0 but 5/80 eval cases failed (OOM or decode errors). :warning:

Alex Chen: Noted. Two leads: (A) the int4 calibration might be per-tensor and losing MLP precision; (B) memory fragmentation from KV growth + batching transient allocations. Can you paste the OOM fragment?

Maria Gomez: OOM snippet from worker-12:
``
[2024-07-06T14:12:03Z] cudaMalloc failed: out of memory
[alloc] requested 134217728 bytes
[meminfo] free: 1.8 GiB, largest_free_block: 512 MiB
[gc] attempted kv-evict -> evicted 0 entries
```

Samir Patel: That meminfo is classic fragmentation — lots of free overall but no contiguous chunk. Happens when KV cache grows and we then allocate big batched tensors. Short-term mitigations: lower the default batch_size to 2 for canary and disable kv-prefetch for the spectral canary.

Lee Nguyen: On the quant side, try an MLP-region int8 fallback. I ran this pattern earlier; it recovers quality in codegen for similar models. Example override:
``
model_overrides:
  - layer_range: [150, 200]
    quant: int8
serve_defaults:
  default_batch_size: 2
  max_new_tokens_default: 128
  kv_prefetch: false
```

Anita Rao: Also re-run calibration with symmetric per-channel quant for int4 and run the focused codegen subset with deterministic RNG to catch token-level regressions. Add a checkerboard eval that targets MLP outputs.

Maria Gomez: I launched two experiments: E1 = batch_size=2 + kv_prefetch=false + int4 per-channel calibration (job 491); E2 = batch_size=4 + MLP layers 150-200 forced int8 + request-level compaction after each call (job 492).

infra-bot: E1 queued on pool-canary-a (a100-32gb), job id 491.
infra-bot: E2 queued on pool-canary-b, job id 492.

Alex Chen: Also flip disable_continuous_batching=true for these canary jobs to avoid mixing seq lengths (that tends to create small holes). If E1 still fails, try tuning allocator thresholds so larger blocks are returned to CUDA sooner.

Samir Patel: Suggested allocator hints:
``
cuda_allocator:
  small_alloc_cutoff: 64k
  large_alloc_cutoff: 16m
  direct_free_threshold: 128m
```
This encourages the runtime to free larger slabs back instead of keeping tiny fragments.

Anita Rao: Early results: E1 recovers most quality (BLEU ~98% of baseline) and no OOMs so far; E2 recovers quality fully (BLEU ~101% vs baseline) but with a 10-15% latency increase. Tradeoff looks like int8 fallback is best for correctness; smaller batch to avoid OOMs.

Lee Nguyen: Proposal: codify profile spectral-7b.quant_profile = "int4-with-mlp-int8", default_batch=2, max_new_tokens=128, kv_prefetch=false. Rollout behind a canary flag with staged percentages.

Maria Gomez: Opening PR with the profile + results and regression artifacts. Plan: merge behind feature flag, ramp 10% -> 50% -> 100% with eval monitors for the first 24h.

ci-bot: PR #2246 opened by maria — spectral-7b: add int4 + mlp-int8 profile, default_batch=2, tests=green.

Alex Chen: I'll review the PR now. :thumbsup:

Maria Gomez: Thanks everyone — will post the final canary metrics once rollout starts. :rocket:
